title: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)
summary: Place accountable human decisions at explicit workflow boundaries, presenting sufficient evidence and preserving approval scope through execution.
overview: Human-in-the-loop architecture asks a person to provide judgment, approval, clarification, or correction at a defined point in an agent workflow. The value comes from matching human responsibility to the decision, not from adding an approve button to every output. Reviewers need the proposed action, relevant evidence, uncertainty, alternatives, and consequences.

Approval is a versioned authorization artifact. Bind it to the exact action and parameters, authenticate the reviewer, and recheck material changes before execution. A human's presence does not guarantee safety: overloaded reviewers can rubber-stamp requests, and poorly designed interfaces can hide the information needed for an informed decision.

production.poc: A prototype can pause and show a proposed action to a domain expert. Observe what evidence the reviewer actually needs to accept or reject it.
production.production: Production creates durable review tasks, role-based assignment, expiry, escalation, and clear reject or edit semantics. Record the approved parameter version and resume through a validated boundary.
production.scale: At scale, prioritize reviews by risk and uncertainty, monitor queue age, and evaluate reviewer disagreement and automation bias. Reserve human attention for decisions where it materially improves the outcome.

components.name: Review trigger
components.role: Determines which conditions require judgment or approval under explicit policy.

components.name: Decision package
components.role: Presents the proposal, source evidence, uncertainty, and expected consequences.

components.name: Review queue
components.role: Assigns work to authorized people and tracks age, escalation, and service expectations.

components.name: Approval record
components.role: Binds the authenticated decision to exact parameters, versions, and validity limits.

components.name: Execution gate
components.role: Rechecks approval scope and current preconditions before performing the action.

flow.title: Detect review condition
flow.description: Apply risk, policy, or uncertainty rules to the proposed next action.

flow.title: Prepare evidence
flow.description: Assemble a concise decision package with inspectable sources and unresolved issues.

flow.title: Suspend durably
flow.description: Persist the waiting state and release active worker resources.

flow.title: Capture decision
flow.description: Authenticate the reviewer and record approve, reject, edit, or request-more-information explicitly.

flow.title: Revalidate scope
flow.description: Compare current parameters and business state with the approved version.

flow.title: Execute or revise
flow.description: Continue only within approval scope, then record the actual outcome for reviewer feedback.

sequenceDiagram

 T-->>G: Authoritative result

diagrams.caption: The execution gate verifies that the action still matches what the reviewer actually approved.

useCase.title: Reviewing an equipment maintenance recommendation
useCase.situation: A utility assistant analyzes maintenance records and proposes taking a pump out of service for inspection.
useCase.problem: A technically plausible recommendation can overlook operational dependencies or current site constraints known to experienced staff.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must support the responsible engineer's decision without directly controlling plant equipment.
useCase.architecture: A review package includes evidence, uncertainty, affected assets, and proposed work-order parameters, with execution restricted to authorized administrative actions.
runtime: The assistant detects a recurring fault pattern and creates a review task instead of issuing an equipment command.
The engineer edits the inspection window; the system validates and records the revised work-order scope before creation.
useCase.failure: If asset status changes after approval, the execution gate pauses and requests renewed review rather than applying stale authorization.
useCase.impact: Track review quality, queue age, parameter changes, stale-approval rejection, and outcomes after review. Human oversight must remain meaningful and adequately supported.

tradeoffs.benefit: Domain judgment can address uncertainty and contextual gaps.
tradeoffs.cost: Human queues add latency and staffing cost.
Small material changes may require another review.
Trigger quality must be evaluated to avoid missed cases.

failures.scenario: A reviewer approves without required authority
failures.detection: Role validation fails at decision capture or execution.
failures.recovery: Reject the approval and reassign the task.

failures.detection: Parameter hash or business version differs.
failures.recovery: Invalidate approval and present the updated decision package.

mistakes.mistake: Showing only the model's confident summary
Treating approval as unlimited future authority
mistakes.fix: Bind it to specific parameters and validity.
Measure workload and reserve mandatory review for meaningful boundaries.

whenToUse: Consequential decisions require accountable human judgment.
Domain context cannot be fully encoded in rules.
A reviewer can inspect evidence before action.
whenNotToUse: The review is ceremonial and cannot affect execution.
No qualified reviewer can respond within the task deadline.
Simple deterministic validation already resolves the issue.
checklist: Monitor queue age and review quality.
